question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> mixture of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>NaOH</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Na</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> and some inert impurities was first titrated with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mi>HCl</mi></math> using phenolphthalein as an indicator, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>17</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>HCl</mi></math> was required at the end point. After this methyl orange was added and titrated. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of same <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>HCl</mi></math> was required for the next end point. The weight percentage of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Na</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> in the mixture is (Rounded-off to the nearest integer)

solution.text:
Upto first end point gm equi. of NaOH+Na2CO3=HCl

x+y×1=110×17.5

x+y=1.75   ....1

Upto second end point

NaOH+Na2CO3≡HCl

x+y×2=110×19

x+2 y=1.9   ....2

y=0.15

%Na2CO3=0.15×10-3×1060.4×100

=3.975%

=4%

Hence answer is 4
